mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals tightening labor market conditions, which increases wage pressures and corporate input costs, leading to reduced profit margins and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%, or the average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates for equities, reducing present value of future cash flows and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the mean 20-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and personal consumption (RSAFS) signals strong underlying demand momentum, which increases corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of joint growth instances, or the Rank IC between the interaction term and SPX 60d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate output and earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0 for two months, or the average 5-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in real personal consumption (RSAFS) following a prior decline signals a recovery in consumer demand, which boosts corporate sales and profit visibility, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 0.5% MoM after two consecutive months of decline
failure_condition: SPX fails to generate positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the mean 20-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a labor market tightening that increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 100k MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp MoM
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC with SPX 20d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A stable or declining CPI (CPIAUCSL) below 190.0 combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) signals disinflationary conditions, which reduce the risk of aggressive rate hikes and support equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both CPIAUCSL < 190.0 and FEDFUNDS < 2.5%, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) at a quarterly rate above 3.0% signals strong aggregate demand growth, which increases corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3.0% qoq, or the mean 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
